17903-writing-the-photoplay.title: Writing The Photoplay
17903-writing-the-photoplay.creator: J. Berg Esenwein
17903-writing-the-photoplay.description: A book by J. Berg Esenwein. As its title indicates, this book aims to teach the theory and practice of photoplay construction. This we shall attempt by first pointing out its component parts, and then showing how these parts are both constructed and assembled so as to form a strong, well-built, attractive and salable manuscript.

arxiv-2012-09875.title: Physics of the Inverted Harmonic Oscillator: From the lowest Landau level to event horizons
arxiv-2012-09875.creator: Varsha Subramanyan, Suraj S. Hegde, Smitha Vishveshwara, Barry Bradlyn
arxiv-2012-09875.description: Abstract In this work, we present the inverted harmonic oscillator (IHO) Hamiltonian as a paradigm to understand the quantum mechanics of scattering and time-decay in a diverse set of physical systems. As one of the generators of area preserving transformations, the IHO Hamiltonian can be studied as a dilatation generator, squeeze generator, a Lorentz boost generator, or a scattering potential.

arxiv-2208-04615.title: A detailed dynamical model for inclination-only dependent lunisolar resonances. Effect on the ”eccentricity growth” mechanism.
arxiv-2208-04615.creator: Edoardo Legnaro, Christos Efthymiopoulos
arxiv-2208-04615.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Edoardo Legnaro, Christos Efthymiopoulos. The focus of this paper is on inclination-only dependent lunisolar resonances, which shape the dynamics of a MEO (Medium Earth Orbit) object over secular time scales (i.e. Following the formalism of daquin2021deep , we discuss an analytical model yielding the correct form of the separatrices of each one of the major lunisolar resonances in the ”action” space ( i , e ) (i,e) (inclination, eccentricity) for any given semi-major axis a a .

arxiv-2210-08890.title: Far-forward production of charm mesons and neutrinos at Forward Physics Facilities at the LHC and the intrinsic charm in the proton
arxiv-2210-08890.creator: Rafał Maciuła, Antoni Szczurek
arxiv-2210-08890.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Rafał Maciuła, Antoni Szczurek. We discuss production of far-forward charm/anticharm quarks, D D mesons/antimesons and neutrinos/antineutrinos from their semileptonic decays in proton-proton collisions at the LHC energies. We include the gluon-gluon fusion g ​ g → c ​ c ¯ gg\to c\bar{c} , the intrinsic charm (IC) g ​ c → g ​ c gc\to gc as well as the recombination g ​ q → D ​ c gq\to Dc partonic mechanisms.

arxiv-2212-10817.title: High-fidelity Direct Contrast Synthesis from Magnetic Resonance Fingerprinting
arxiv-2212-10817.creator: Ke Wang *, Mariya Doneva, Jakob Meineke, Thomas Amthor, Ekin Karasan, Fei Tan, Jonathan I. Tamir, Stella X. Yu, Michael Lustig
arxiv-2212-10817.description: Abstract Magnetic Resonance Fingerprinting (MRF) is an efficient quantitative MRI technique that can extract important tissue and system parameters such as T1, T2, B0, and B1 from a single scan. This property also makes it attractive for retrospectively synthesizing contrast-weighted images. In general, contrast-weighted images like T1-weighted, T2-weighted, etc.

arxiv-2304-03570.title: Towards Automated 3D Search Planning for Emergency Response Missions Thanks: The authors are with the KIOS Research and Innovation Centre of Excellence (KIOS CoE) and the Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering, University of Cyprus, Nicosia, 1678, Cyprus. {papaioannou.savvas, pkolios, tth
arxiv-2304-03570.creator: Savvas Papaioannou, Panayiotis Kolios, Theocharis Theocharides
arxiv-2304-03570.description: Abstract The ability to efficiently plan and execute automated and precise search missions using unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) during emergency response situations is imperative. Precise navigation between obstacles and time-efficient searching of 3D structures and buildings are essential for locating survivors and people in need in emergency response missions.

arxiv-2306-01682.title: Impacts of the C 12 ​ ( α , γ ) 16 ​ O {}^{12}{\rm C}(\alpha,\gamma)^{16}{\rm O}\, reaction rate on Ni 56 {}^{56}\mathrm{Ni} nucleosynthesis in pair-instability supernovae 2024 Impacts of the C 12 ​ ( α , γ ) 16 ​ O {}^{12}{\rm C}(\alpha,\gamma)^{16}{\rm O}\, reaction rate on Ni 56 {}^{56}\mathrm{Ni
arxiv-2306-01682.creator: Hiroki Kawashimo, Ryo Sawada, Yudai Suwa Takashi J. Moriya, Ataru Tanikawa, Nozomu Tominaga
arxiv-2306-01682.description: Abstract Nuclear reactions are key to our understanding of stellar evolution, particularly the C 12 ​ ( α , γ ) 16 ​ O {}^{12}{\rm C}(\alpha,\gamma)^{16}{\rm O}\, rate, which is known to significantly influence the lower and upper ends of the black hole (BH) mass distribution due to pair-instability supernovae (PISNe). However, these reaction rates have not been sufficiently determined.

arxiv-2306-02034.title: Does Microservices Adoption Impact the Development Velocity? A Cohort Study
arxiv-2306-02034.creator: Nyyti Saarimäki, Mikel Robredo, Sira Vegas, Natalia Juristo, Davide Taibi, Valentina Lenarduzzi
arxiv-2306-02034.description: Abstract . [Context] Microservices enable the decomposition of applications into small and independent services connected together. The independence between services could positively affect the development velocity of a project, which is considered an important metric measuring the time taken to implement features and fix bugs. However, no studies have investigated the connection between microservices and development velocity.

arxiv-2402-06617.title: FaBERT: Pre-training BERT on Persian Blogs
arxiv-2402-06617.creator: Mostafa Masumi, Seyed Soroush Majd, Mehrnoush Shamsfard, Hamid Beigy
arxiv-2402-06617.description: Abstract We introduce FaBERT, a Persian BERT-base model pre-trained on the HmBlogs corpus, encompassing both informal and formal Persian texts. FaBERT is designed to excel in traditional Natural Language Understanding (NLU) tasks, addressing the intricacies of diverse sentence structures and linguistic styles prevalent in the Persian language.

arxiv-2501-18366.title: Active rheology of soft solids performed with acoustical tweezers
arxiv-2501-18366.creator: Antoine Penneron, Thomas Brunet, Diego Baresch
arxiv-2501-18366.description: Abstract Single-beam acoustical tweezers are used to manipulate individual microbubbles and provide quantitative measurements of the local shear modulus of soft hydrogels. The microbubbles are directly generated by electrolysis of the hydrogel and their displacement is detected using optical microscopy in the focal plane of a focused vortex beam.

arxiv-2503-06301.title: Driven Magnon-Photon System as a Tunable Quantum Heat Rectifier
arxiv-2503-06301.creator: C. O. Edet, K. Słowik, N. Ali, M. Asjad, O. Abah
arxiv-2503-06301.description: Abstract Controlling heat flow at the quantum level is a key challenge for next-generation quantum technologies, including thermal management and quantum information processing. Here, we investigate quantum heat transport in an asymmetrically driven hybrid magnon-photon system in contact with two thermal baths at different temperatures.

arxiv-2504-14569.title: NoWag: A Unified Framework for Shape Preserving Compression of Large Language Models
arxiv-2504-14569.creator: Lawrence Liu, Inesh Chakrabarti, Yixiao Li, Mengdi Wang, Tuo Zhao, Lin F. Yang
arxiv-2504-14569.description: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) exhibit remarkable performance across various natural language processing tasks but suffer from immense computational and memory demands, limiting their deployment in resource-constrained environments. To address this challenge, we propose NoWag ( No rmalized W eight and A ctivation Guided Compression), a unified framework for one-shot shape preserving compression algorithms.

arxiv-2508-05714.description: Abstract This paper establishes that, under the appropriate range of values of the parameters involved in the formulation of the model, a diffusive predator-prey system with saturation can have an arbitrarily large number of coexistence states for sufficiently large saturation rates.

pmc-11289381.title: Human-centred physical neuromorphics with visual brain-computer interfaces
pmc-11289381.creator: Gao Wang, Giulia Marcucci, Benjamin Peters, Maria Chiara Braidotti, Lars Muckli, Daniele Faccio
pmc-11289381.description: Steady-state visual evoked potentials (SSVEPs) are widely used for brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) as they provide a stable and efficient means to connect the computer to the brain with a simple flickering light. Previous studies focused on low-density frequency division multiplexing techniques, i.e. typically employing one or two light-modulation frequencies during a single flickering light stimulation.

pmc-11503078.title: Prevalence of Mycoplasma genitalium and macrolide resistance in rectal and urine samples among men who have sex with men in Sweden
pmc-11503078.creator: Carina Bjartling, Rebecca Kertes, Sinja Kristiansen, Annika Johnsson, Ola Forslund
pmc-11503078.description: AbstractObjectivesWhile Mycoplasma genitalium is reported as a common rectal infection among men who have sex with men (MSM), published data refer predominantly to urethral infections. Currently, most guidelines recommend M. genitalium testing from urine in men with symptomatic, non-gonococcal urethritis. Macrolide resistance-associated mutations (MRMs) among M. genitalium have increased during the last decade especially among MSM.

pmc-11740749.title: Physicochemical Properties of Sago- and Corn Flour-Based Rice Analogues Fortified with Black-Eyed Bean Flour and Skimmed Milk Powder
pmc-11740749.creator: Noer Abyor Handayani, Siswo Sumardiono, Aprilina Purbasari, Alfan Fatir Fatikah, Imam Muda Alhakim
pmc-11740749.description: SUMMARYResearch backgroundWith the increasing consumption of food commodities, particularly rice, and the substantial volume of food imports in Indonesia, there is an increasing need to explore alternative food sources. Rice analogues emerge as a potential substitute for traditional rice, serving as a viable staple food option.

pmc-13334560.title: Use of emergency medical services by adults with developmental disabilities receiving integrated or usual care
pmc-13334560.creator: Daniel Gilmore, Emily Johnson, Lauren Wang, Corey Keeton, Aurora Rivendale, Susan M. Havercamp, Lindy L. Weaver, Ingrid Adams, Brittany N. Hand
pmc-13334560.description: Background:Adults with developmental disabilities (DD) frequently utilize the emergency department (ED) and are hospitalized for psychiatric emergencies. Community healthcare models like integrated care where primary care and mental health services are co-located may better meet the needs of adults with DD and reduce use of emergency services.

pmc-13377778.title: Mycobacterium tuberculosis-induced PCBP1 degradation drives macrophage ferroptosis to promote infection: a lung-macrophage-targeted RNAa nanotherapy
pmc-13377778.creator: Huan-Shao Huang, Jia-Xin Chi, Jia-Jun Wang, Le-Yao Xiao, Lan Chen, Shi-Ying Lai, Wan-Yi Liu, Feng Yang, Kang-Sheng Liao, Jiang Pi, Yan-Guang Cong, Yi-Ming Shao, Jun-Fa Xu
pmc-13377778.description: BackgroundImmune evasion by Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) complicates tuberculosis (TB) therapy. Ferroptosis, an iron-dependent form of regulated cell death, is increasingly recognized as a critical process in host-pathogen interactions. We aimed to define the role of poly(C)-binding protein 1 (PCBP1) in macrophage ferroptosis during Mtb infection and to develop a targeted RNA activation (RNAa) nanotherapy to exploit this pathway.

pmc-13476350.creator: Lars-Jøran Andersson, Gunnar Skov Simonsen, Erik Solligård, Knut Fredriksen

PurposeTo describe the epidemiology of blood cultures (BCs) drawn from patients with suspected sepsis by a rural ambulance service.MethodsPatients were included if they had clinically suspected sepsis and at least one BC was drawn.

pmc-13579833.title: The association between hyperlipidemia and colorectal adenoma risk: a multivariable clinical study based on lipoprotein profile stratification
pmc-13579833.creator: Wei Wen, Longfei Liao, Kaixi Ou, Chongling Liu
pmc-13579833.description: BackgroundThe incidence of colorectal cancer (CRC) continues to rise, with colorectal adenoma(CRA) being its primary precancerous lesion. Recent studies suggest that hyperlipidemia may promote adenoma development by influencing cell membrane structure, cholesterol metabolism, and inflammatory responses. However, its independent role in the adenoma stage remains unclear.
